Thanks all — quick legal perspective and what we need from Novaproc to keep to the proposed cadence.

Scope: please confirm which documents are in-scope for redlines in this MAP: MSA (master services agreement), DPA (data processing agreement), and SLA (operational targets). I will assume all three unless you advise otherwise.

Evidence / inputs we need to accept any expedited review:
- SOC 2 report (most recent) or equivalent audit summary.
- Data residency requirement (region(s) and account-level restrictions).
- KMS/HSM requirements if you require customer-managed keys — outline expected key lifecycle and rotations.
- Any regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR data processor details, PCI scope).

Turnaround expectation (Redwood legal internal):
- Initial review (non-expedited): 3 business days (covers MSA + SLA).
- DPA review: up to 5 business days for substantive DPA edits (often requires privacy counsel).
- Expedited: 48 hours for items labeled P1 in the MAP (security, data residency, breach notification).

If Novaproc confirms that P1 items are limited to a short list, we will accept 48h for those; otherwise we reserve 3-5bd for fuller reviews.

I've attached a legal-evidence-checklist.docx to make it easy for your procurement/legal to provide what we need. If Sophie can drop the list of redline priorities, I'll commit to calendar blocks for expedited reviews next week.
